questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted somewhere, where I knew the language so I could get around and bond with the locals easily.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a little harder than I expected to bond with the local students, especially if you dont live on campus or in uni accommodation. I lived in a flat in the city but with people on working holiday visas so I only got to bond with the locals in class, which was a little hard cause they often have very individual courses on the undergrad (bachelor) so its not one class you stay with its four different classes.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: very easy - Monash sent me heaps of emails

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were some information days before classes started for all the exchange/international students

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found a big flat with six other young people on working holiday visas through a facebook page called 'Fairy Floss Real Estate'

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I liked it cause i arrived two months before uni started so it gave me time to settle in before hand and to be closer to the city - but once uni started it was a little harder cause all the arranged activities were on campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had heard a lot of bad things, like it being very expensive and not clean, but I didn't research it a lot

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Be aware that in January (for semester 1) you can change around your classes - I ended up only having classes Monday - Wednesday

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get an email on your monash student email that explains it and there is a video guide as well

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: the website is pretty helpful

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful - I moved around my classes so i had long weekends Thursday - Monday

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure your classes are on campus rather than online

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level depended on the class - i had classes with first years which was fairly easy, but also classes with third years which was a bit more challenging. My exchange was the last semester of my BA

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was much more class room style and a lot of group work which i enjoyed - The teacher also asks a lot of questions out to the class so you had to be prepared to engage in class. There were also weekly quizzes in two of my classes, which you has to pass to pass the class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ATS1089 – Fundamentals of journalism
ATS2324 – Climate change communication
ATS3789 – Documentary
ATS1125 – Public relations foundations

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really enjoyed Climate change communication and documentary! 

Climate change communication was very interesting especially because climate change is a big topic of debate in Australia, plus the final assignment was very creative and a good use of the practical skills we learned in class. 

Documentary was really fun - we had a lot of solo responsibilities and learned a lot just by trial and error. The teacher was very enthusiastic and helped a lot with useful feedback, and for the final assessment you make a short 5-7 documentary on your own which was a really fun project and very useful for future

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Doctor appointments are quite expensive, but you get the money back from insurance

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is pretty much the same as in Copenhagen I would say - expect for sushi which is very cheap and can be found everywhere!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really join to many clubs but there was a lot of different ones you could have joined

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I joined the outdoor club and surf club which was a lot of fun!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would join the surf club so you can go surfing and camping!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I went to Sydney, Perth and Uluru on long weekends - Uluru was amazing and I would 100% recommend everyone to go there! We went on a group tour with a lot of young people and a guide and even through it was quite expensive it was worth all the money!

I also went on a months trip to New Zealand, and ended my exchange with a week in Bali and a week in South Korea! My advice: Take advantage of being to close to countries that are normally super expensive to go to.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the Australians are very similar to the Danes

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There is quite a lot of underlying racism, which the younger generation definitely is dealing with a lot better than the older generation, but it is quite noticeable in their culture in general

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed learning more about the first nation peoples

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
If you are a BA student you can get a concession card for the public transport and get 50% of, which saves you A LOT
Pick classes that sound fun and try to get the aligned so you can have long weekends free to do trips
Befriend someone with a car! It makes it a lot easier to get around and to go on trips

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont be afraid to speak up in class - often the teacher is interested in the point of view you can bring from your country

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Seeing so much of a country that is so fare away

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: connecting with the aussies - a lot of them stick to the friends they have from high school so it can be a little tricky to make friends

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
